name: ORB-SLAM2
summary: Feature-based SLAM for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras using ORB features, with loop closing and relocalization against a reusable map.
why_it_matters: The reference visual SLAM baseline most papers compare against; cheap camera-only localization when GNSS is denied.
hackathon_notes: Superseded by ORB-SLAM3 and no longer developed; builds need patching on modern OpenCV/Eigen. Use only to reproduce old baselines.

name: ORB-SLAM3
summary: Visual, visual-inertial and multi-map SLAM supporting monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras with pinhole and fisheye models, using a map atlas to survive tracking loss.
why_it_matters: Still the most cited open VI-SLAM system; a solid GNSS-denied drift baseline for drones and ground robots.
hackathon_notes: Build against Pangolin, OpenCV and Eigen; expect a few compile fixes. Run on EuRoC or TUM-VI first, then your own camera after Kalibr calibration. Upstream sees little activity.

name: ORB_SLAM3_ROS2
summary: ROS 2 wrapper package that exposes ORB-SLAM3 as nodes for monocular, stereo and RGB-D input.
why_it_matters: Shortest path to running ORB-SLAM3 inside a ROS 2 robot stack.
hackathon_notes: Needs a working ORB-SLAM3 build first; check the README for the ROS 2 distro it targets before choosing your Docker base image.

name: VINS-Mono
summary: Optimization-based monocular visual-inertial estimator with sliding-window bundle adjustment, online initialization, loop closure and pose-graph reuse.
why_it_matters: The canonical one-camera-plus-IMU estimator; works on light UAV payloads where stereo or LiDAR is too heavy.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 only and no longer maintained; run in a Melodic/Noetic container. Sensitive to time sync and initialization motion.

name: VINS-Fusion
summary: Extension of VINS-Mono supporting mono+IMU, stereo, and stereo+IMU, with optional loose fusion of global sensors such as GPS.
why_it_matters: Shows how to plug intermittent GNSS into a VIO estimator, which is the core pattern for degraded-PNT navigation.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; use a Docker image. The global-fusion node is a good template for injecting GNSS when it is trusted and dropping it when jammed.

name: OpenVINS
summary: MSCKF-based visual-inertial navigation platform with online calibration, a simulator, and extensive documentation for research use.
why_it_matters: Probably the best-documented VIO codebase; filter-based, light enough for embedded boards.
hackathon_notes: Supports ROS 1 and ROS 2. Its built-in simulator lets you test without hardware on day one. Docs site explains every estimator component.

name: MINS
summary: Multi-sensor aided inertial navigation that fuses IMU with camera, LiDAR, GNSS and wheel odometry, including online spatial/temporal calibration and a multi-sensor simulator.
why_it_matters: Directly relevant to assured PNT: one estimator that degrades gracefully as individual sensors (including GNSS) drop out.
hackathon_notes: Start with the provided simulated data to see each sensor's contribution, then disable GNSS mid-run to demo a jamming scenario.

name: Kimera-VIO
summary: Stereo visual-inertial odometry with a factor-graph backend, robust loop closure and real-time 3D mesh generation; the odometry core of the Kimera stack.
why_it_matters: Gives both a pose and a lightweight 3D mesh, useful for situational-awareness displays.
hackathon_notes: Heavier build (GTSAM, OpenGV, DBoW2); use the Docker setup. The ROS wrapper lives in a separate repo.

name: Kimera-RPGO
summary: Robust pose-graph optimization that rejects bad loop closures via pairwise consistency maximization on top of GTSAM.
why_it_matters: Outlier-robust loop closure is what keeps a long GNSS-denied mission from corrupting its map; reusable outside Kimera.
hackathon_notes: Small library; feed it any odometry + loop closure edges. Good drop-in back end for a custom front end.

name: Basalt
summary: GitHub mirror of Basalt, a visual-inertial odometry and mapping system built around non-linear factor recovery, with calibration tools; primary development is on GitLab.
why_it_matters: Fast, accurate stereo VIO that runs well on CPUs; also ships camera-IMU calibration.
hackathon_notes: Submit issues upstream on GitLab. Builds cleanly on Ubuntu; ROS integration is via community wrappers.

name: SVO Pro
summary: Open release of SVO Pro: semi-direct visual(-inertial) odometry with fisheye/omni camera support, optional global map and loop closure.
why_it_matters: Very low-latency front end suited to fast agile flight on compute-limited drones.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 / catkin build; dormant since 2024. Good when CPU budget is tight.

name: DSO (Direct Sparse Odometry)
summary: Direct monocular visual odometry that optimizes photometric error over a sparse set of pixels with joint photometric calibration.
why_it_matters: Works in low-texture scenes where feature-based methods fail; the basis for DM-VIO and many direct methods.
hackathon_notes: No IMU, no loop closure, scale-ambiguous; mostly useful as a building block or comparison.

name: DM-VIO
summary: Monocular visual-inertial odometry built on DSO using delayed marginalization and pose-graph bundle adjustment for IMU initialization.
why_it_matters: Strong monocular VIO accuracy; good for single-camera drones.
hackathon_notes: Standalone build with an optional ROS wrapper repo. Expects photometrically calibrated input for best results.

name: ROVIO
summary: Robust visual-inertial odometry using an iterated EKF directly on image-patch photometric errors.
why_it_matters: Long a go-to VIO on PX4/MAV research platforms because it is cheap to run.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 / catkin. Lightweight; tuning of patch and feature counts matters.

name: MSCKF_VIO
summary: Stereo multi-state constraint Kalman filter VIO designed for fast autonomous flight.
why_it_matters: Lean filter-based stereo VIO that runs comfortably on embedded CPUs.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; unmaintained. Tested heavily on EuRoC; good comparison point to OpenVINS.

name: OKVIS2
summary: Keyframe-based visual-inertial SLAM with loop closure and a realtime scalable factor-graph design; second generation of OKVIS.
why_it_matters: Mature research VI-SLAM from the ETH/TUM lineage with active maintenance.
hackathon_notes: CMake build; check the README for ROS integration and the camera/IMU config format for your sensor.

name: OKVIS2-X
summary: Extension of OKVIS2 that can additionally use dense depth or LiDAR and fuse GNSS.
why_it_matters: Recent (2025-2026) multi-sensor VI-SLAM that includes GNSS fusion, matching assured-PNT architectures.
hackathon_notes: New codebase; expect some setup friction. Good showcase for switching GNSS on/off.

name: AirSLAM
summary: Point-and-line visual(-inertial) SLAM using learned features, designed for illumination-robust operation, with TensorRT acceleration; successor to AirVO.
why_it_matters: Targets lighting changes (dawn/dusk/night), a common failure mode for camera navigation.
hackathon_notes: Needs an NVIDIA GPU (TensorRT). Docker recommended.

name: maplab
summary: Modular multi-session, multi-modal mapping framework with map merging, optimization and localization against saved maps.
why_it_matters: Build a map once, then localize repeatedly against it; supports multi-robot and multi-session merges.
hackathon_notes: Large ROS 1 codebase; only worth it if you need persistent map management.

name: RTAB-Map
summary: Graph-based SLAM library and app supporting RGB-D, stereo and LiDAR, with memory management for large-scale loop closure and map reuse.
why_it_matters: Practical all-rounder with GUI, database and localization modes; easiest way to get a working 3D map on a ground robot.
hackathon_notes: Install via apt binaries (ROS) or the standalone app. Supports phone/iPad LiDAR capture. Save a map, then switch to localization mode.

name: rtabmap_ros
summary: ROS and ROS 2 integration for RTAB-Map, exposing SLAM, localization and odometry nodes.
why_it_matters: Drop-in SLAM for ROS 2 Nav2 stacks.
hackathon_notes: apt-installable for supported distros; launch examples cover common sensors.

name: DROID-SLAM
summary: Deep visual SLAM that iterates dense bundle adjustment through a recurrent update operator, for monocular, stereo and RGB-D input.
why_it_matters: Much more robust than classic pipelines on hard sequences; strong learned baseline.
hackathon_notes: Needs a large-memory NVIDIA GPU; not real-time on embedded. Pretrained weights available.

name: DPVO / DPV-SLAM
summary: Deep Patch Visual Odometry: learned sparse patch tracking for VO, plus DPV-SLAM with loop closure.
why_it_matters: Lighter learned VO than DROID-SLAM, closer to real-time on a desktop GPU.
hackathon_notes: CUDA build of custom kernels; follow the conda instructions.

name: MASt3R-SLAM
summary: Real-time dense monocular SLAM built on the MASt3R two-view 3D reconstruction prior, needing no fixed camera model (CVPR 2025).
why_it_matters: Works with uncalibrated cameras, useful for opportunistic imagery from unknown cameras.
hackathon_notes: Requires a capable NVIDIA GPU and model checkpoint downloads. Great demo value on handheld video.

name: VGGT
summary: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer: a feed-forward network predicting camera poses, depth and point maps from one or many images (CVPR 2025 best paper).
why_it_matters: Instant pose and geometry from a handful of frames; a building block for learned relocalization and mapping.
hackathon_notes: GPU inference via PyTorch; Hugging Face demo for quick tests. Not a full SLAM system by itself.

name: MonoGS (Gaussian Splatting SLAM)
summary: Gaussian-splatting SLAM for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras that tracks and maps directly against a 3D Gaussian representation.
why_it_matters: Produces photorealistic maps useful for operator situational awareness and later simulation.
hackathon_notes: Needs a strong GPU; not real-time on embedded hardware. Best as an offline mapping demo.

name: SplaTAM
summary: Dense RGB-D SLAM that tracks and maps using 3D Gaussians and differentiable rendering (CVPR 2024).
why_it_matters: Reference Gaussian-splatting SLAM for RGB-D sensors.
hackathon_notes: GPU-heavy and slower than real time; good for offline indoor captures.

name: Photo-SLAM
summary: Couples ORB-SLAM3-style geometric tracking with a photorealistic Gaussian map for monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras (CVPR 2024).
why_it_matters: Classic robust tracking plus a nice-looking map, closer to real time than pure splatting SLAM.
hackathon_notes: LibTorch + CUDA build; check version pins carefully.

name: ESVO
summary: Event-based stereo visual odometry using spatio-temporal consistency of two event cameras for mapping and tracking.
why_it_matters: Event cameras keep working under high dynamic range and fast motion, where frame cameras blur or saturate.
hackathon_notes: Needs stereo event cameras or recorded datasets; ROS 1.

name: Ultimate SLAM
summary: Open-source release of Ultimate SLAM, combining events, standard frames and IMU for VIO in HDR and high-speed scenarios (RA-L 2018).
why_it_matters: Template for fusing event cameras with frames and IMU for robust flight state estimation.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 / catkin; test on event datasets before buying hardware.

name: Event-based Vision Resources
summary: Community-curated list of event-camera papers, datasets, drivers, simulators and code.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to find event-camera datasets and odometry code.
hackathon_notes: Use as a discovery index; not runnable code.

name: HKU Event-based VO/VIO/SLAM
summary: Dataset and index of event-based VO, VIO and SLAM work from HKU ArcLab, including stereo event sequences.
why_it_matters: Ready-made event data for testing event odometry without hardware.
hackathon_notes: Download sequences as rosbags; pair with ESVO.

name: ROVTIO
summary: Visual-thermal-inertial odometry extending ROVIO to fuse asynchronous thermal and visual images with IMU, switching to whichever camera is informative.
why_it_matters: Thermal keeps odometry alive in darkness and smoke; NTNU ARL targets subterranean and degraded environments.
hackathon_notes: Needs a thermal camera synced to IMU (or their datasets). Thermal calibration targets need a heated pattern.

name: ETIO
summary: Edge-based monocular thermal-inertial odometry that tracks thermal edges for visually degraded environments.
why_it_matters: Low-cost night/smoke navigation from a single thermal camera plus IMU.
hackathon_notes: Code released with the paper; try on public thermal datasets first.

name: RRxIO
summary: Radar visual/thermal inertial odometry fusing 4D mmWave radar with a visual or thermal camera and IMU for degraded visual conditions.
why_it_matters: Radar plus thermal is a strong combination for fog, smoke and darkness.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; datasets released by the author. Good for a degraded-visibility demo.

name: RIO
summary: EKF-based radar-inertial odometry using 4D mmWave radar ego-velocity measurements.
why_it_matters: Cheap automotive radars give velocity in fog/smoke/darkness; a minimal radar odometry template.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; uses the author's radar ego-velocity estimator. Works with TI mmWave-class sensors.

name: 4DRadarSLAM
summary: 4D radar SLAM with scan-to-scan registration, loop closure and pose-graph optimization, released with an NTU 4D radar dataset.
why_it_matters: One of the few full SLAM pipelines for 4D imaging radar, the all-weather sensor for ground vehicles.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; structured like hdl_graph_slam. Test on their dataset first.

name: CFEAR Radarodometry
summary: Learning-free spinning-radar odometry that filters returns to sparse oriented surface points and registers against keyframes.
why_it_matters: Strong baseline for spinning (Navtech-style) radar odometry; robust in weather that defeats LiDAR.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; benchmarked on Oxford Radar RobotCar and Boreas.

name: Go-RIO
summary: Ground-optimized 4D radar-inertial odometry integrating continuous velocity via Gaussian processes (ICRA 2025 best paper finalist).
why_it_matters: Recent state of the art for 4D radar odometry on ground vehicles.
hackathon_notes: Recent code; check sensor assumptions against your radar.

name: Gaussian-RIO
summary: 4D radar-inertial odometry using Gaussian modeling of radar points and multi-hypothesis scan matching.
why_it_matters: Another recent open 4D radar odometry baseline, useful for comparison.
hackathon_notes: Small research codebase; read the paper before integrating.

name: LIO-SAM
summary: Tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial odometry via factor-graph smoothing, with optional GPS factors and loop closure.
why_it_matters: Popular LIO with built-in GNSS factors; the template for LiDAR+INS+intermittent GNSS.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 main branch, community ROS 2 branch. Needs a 9-axis IMU and careful extrinsics.

name: FAST-LIO / FAST-LIO2
summary: Computationally efficient LiDAR-inertial odometry using an iterated error-state Kalman filter and incremental k-d tree map, mapping raw points directly.
why_it_matters: The default LIO in many field robots; runs on ARM boards and supports solid-state and spinning LiDARs.
hackathon_notes: Easiest LIO to get running; Livox drivers supported. No loop closure; pair with a localization or loop-closure add-on.

name: Point-LIO
summary: High-bandwidth LiDAR-inertial odometry that updates the state point by point, tolerating aggressive motion and IMU saturation.
why_it_matters: Handles violent motion (agile drones, vibration) where frame-based LIO breaks.
hackathon_notes: Same ecosystem as FAST-LIO; try when FAST-LIO diverges on aggressive motion.

name: FAST-LIVO2
summary: Direct LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry fusing LiDAR, camera and IMU in a sequential ESIKF update with a unified voxel map.
why_it_matters: High-accuracy colored mapping that stays robust when either LiDAR or camera degrades.
hackathon_notes: Needs hardware-synced LiDAR+camera; datasets available.

name: R3LIVE
summary: Tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial-visual estimation and RGB-colored mapping package.
why_it_matters: Produces dense colored maps useful for operator displays and mapping.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1, heavy on dependencies; FAST-LIVO2 is the newer alternative.

name: LI-Init
summary: Real-time LiDAR-IMU initialization estimating temporal offset and extrinsics without a calibration target.
why_it_matters: Removes the extrinsic-calibration blocker when bolting a LiDAR and IMU onto a new platform.
hackathon_notes: Wave the rig around for a minute; feed results into FAST-LIO.

name: KISS-ICP
summary: Minimal LiDAR odometry based on point-to-point ICP with adaptive thresholding, working across sensors with few parameters.
why_it_matters: Works out of the box on almost any LiDAR without IMU; ideal hackathon starting point.
hackathon_notes: `pip install kiss-icp` and run on a rosbag or KITTI folder in minutes. Add KISS-SLAM for loop closure.

name: KISS-SLAM
summary: LiDAR SLAM that adds loop closure and pose-graph optimization on top of KISS-ICP odometry.
why_it_matters: Full LiDAR SLAM with the same low-configuration philosophy.
hackathon_notes: Pip-installable; quick to demo on outdoor bags.

name: MapClosures
summary: Loop-closure detection using bird's-eye-view density images of local LiDAR maps.
why_it_matters: Sensor-agnostic loop closure that plugs into any LiDAR odometry.
hackathon_notes: Python bindings via pip.

name: RKO-LIO
summary: LiDAR-inertial odometry aiming to work without sensor-specific modelling or heavy tuning.
why_it_matters: Recent (2025-2026) LIO from the KISS-ICP group; good for unknown hardware.
hackathon_notes: `pip install "rko_lio[all]"` then `rko_lio -v /path/to/bags` runs on ROS 1 or ROS 2 bags with a rerun viewer; a ROS 2 node is also available. You must supply IMU and LiDAR extrinsics if the bag's TF tree lacks them. No loop closure - see rko_slam for that.

name: LeGO-LOAM
summary: Lightweight ground-optimized LiDAR odometry and mapping that segments ground to speed up feature extraction on UGVs.
why_it_matters: Classic UGV LiDAR SLAM for rough terrain on modest compute.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 only, unmaintained, tuned for Velodyne VLP-16. Use LIO-SAM or KISS-ICP instead unless reproducing baselines.

name: Cartographer
summary: Real-time 2D and 3D SLAM with submaps and branch-and-bound loop closure across many sensor configurations.
why_it_matters: Widely deployed 2D LiDAR SLAM for indoor and warehouse robots.
hackathon_notes: Project is in maintenance mode with little activity. Still available via ROS packages and works for 2D indoor mapping.

name: GLIM
summary: Versatile point-cloud localization and mapping framework with GPU-accelerated factor graphs, supporting many range sensors and optional IMU.
why_it_matters: Modern, maintained 3D mapping with GPU speedups and an extensible module system.
hackathon_notes: Prebuilt packages exist for ROS 2; GPU optional but recommended.

name: fast_gicp
summary: Collection of fast GICP and VGICP point-cloud registration implementations, multithreaded and CUDA.
why_it_matters: Fast scan registration building block used by many LiDAR and radar SLAM systems.
hackathon_notes: Successor library small_gicp is more actively maintained.

name: small_gicp
summary: Efficient, parallel point-cloud registration library (GICP, ICP variants) with C++ and Python APIs.
why_it_matters: Pip-installable registration to build your own LiDAR odometry or map-based relocalization fast.
hackathon_notes: `pip install small_gicp`; good for scan-to-map localization prototypes.

name: Faster-LIO
summary: Lightweight tightly coupled LiDAR-inertial odometry using parallel sparse incremental voxels instead of a k-d tree.
why_it_matters: Faster variant of the FAST-LIO design for constrained compute.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; same config style as FAST-LIO.

name: DLIO
summary: Lightweight LiDAR-inertial odometry with coarse-to-fine continuous-time motion correction (ICRA 2023).
why_it_matters: Accurate and compute-light LIO for aerial and ground robots.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 main; check community ROS 2 forks.

name: FAST_LIO_LOCALIZATION
summary: Relocalization in a prebuilt map using FAST-LIO odometry plus global scan-to-map registration.
why_it_matters: Localize in a map you surveyed earlier, the standard pattern for GNSS-denied ground ops in known areas.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; build a map with FAST-LIO first, then localize. Needs a rough initial pose (RViz or another sensor). The global-localization node needs Python 2.7 and Open3D 0.9, so plan for a Melodic-era environment or a container.

name: Scan Context
summary: LiDAR global place descriptor for loop detection and relocalization (backup of the original IRAP KAIST repo).
why_it_matters: Simple, widely used LiDAR loop-closure descriptor; plugs into most LiDAR SLAM.
hackathon_notes: Header-only style C++; SC-LIO-SAM shows integration.

name: SC-LIO-SAM
summary: LIO-SAM combined with Scan Context loop closure for more reliable large-scale LiDAR-inertial SLAM.
why_it_matters: Practical recipe for adding a global descriptor to an existing LIO.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; same setup as LIO-SAM.

name: STD
summary: Stable Triangle Descriptor for 3D point-cloud place recognition and loop closure.
why_it_matters: Works with solid-state LiDARs and small fields of view where Scan Context struggles.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 demos; integrates with FAST-LIO.

name: TEASER++
summary: Certifiable, outlier-robust point-cloud registration library with C++, Python and MATLAB bindings.
why_it_matters: Global registration that tolerates extreme outlier rates, useful for map-to-map alignment and relocalization.
hackathon_notes: Needs correspondences (e.g. FPFH) as input; Python bindings make it quick to prototype.

name: Quatro
summary: Fast, robust global registration for terrestrial robots that assumes near-planar motion to cut degrees of freedom.
why_it_matters: Faster global relocalization for ground vehicles.
hackathon_notes: Smaller research codebase; pair with KISS-ICP.

name: MIMOSA
summary: Tightly coupled sliding-window factor-graph fusion of IMU with LiDAR (geometric and photometric), radar radial-speed factors and external odometry such as VIO.
why_it_matters: From the group behind DARPA SubT field robots; relevant to smoke/dark/dust scenarios.
hackathon_notes: ROS Noetic; publishes nav_msgs/Odometry. Radar factor lets you keep velocity constraints when LiDAR is blinded by dust or smoke.

name: livox_ros_driver2
summary: ROS 1/ROS 2 driver for Livox LiDARs such as Mid-360 and HAP.
why_it_matters: Mid-360 is a common cheap LiDAR for drones; you need this driver to feed FAST-LIO and friends.
hackathon_notes: Build with the Livox SDK2; set the custom message format expected by FAST-LIO.

name: hdl_graph_slam
summary: 3D LiDAR graph SLAM with NDT/GICP scan matching odometry, loop detection and optional GPS, IMU and floor-plane constraints.
why_it_matters: Simple, hackable graph SLAM that 4DRadarSLAM and others build on; GPS constraints make it handy for mixed GNSS/denied runs.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1; GLIM is the author's newer framework.

name: Kimera-Multi
summary: Index repo for Kimera-Multi, a distributed multi-robot metric-semantic SLAM system with robust distributed pose-graph optimization.
why_it_matters: Multi-robot mapping with peer-to-peer communication is core to swarm and team operations.
hackathon_notes: Multi-repo install; budget a full day. Use their datasets for a demo.

name: Kimera-Distributed
summary: Distributed back end of Kimera-Multi handling inter-robot loop closures and distributed optimization.
why_it_matters: Reusable distributed SLAM back end.
hackathon_notes: Used through Kimera-Multi.

name: DPGO
summary: Distributed pose-graph optimization library with certifiably correct solutions for multi-robot SLAM.
why_it_matters: Solver core for decentralized multi-robot SLAM.
hackathon_notes: Library only; feed it pose graphs from each robot.

name: Swarm-SLAM
summary: ROS 2 decentralized collaborative SLAM supporting LiDAR, stereo and RGB-D, with sparse inter-robot communication.
why_it_matters: Designed for bandwidth-limited swarms, a realistic constraint under jamming.
hackathon_notes: ROS 2; experiments run on recorded multi-robot datasets. Pick one sensor type to start.

name: COVINS / COVINS-G
summary: Centralized collaborative visual-inertial SLAM where agents run VIO and a server merges maps; COVINS-G is VIO-front-end agnostic.
why_it_matters: Pattern for drones sharing maps through a ground station.
hackathon_notes: ROS 1 + Docker; COVINS-G can take poses from any VIO such as OpenVINS.

name: D2SLAM
summary: Decentralized and distributed collaborative visual-inertial SLAM for aerial swarms.
why_it_matters: Swarm-scale relative localization and mapping for UAV teams.
hackathon_notes: Heavy setup; mainly useful as a design reference.

name: evo
summary: Python package and CLI for evaluating odometry and SLAM trajectories (ATE/RPE, alignment, plotting) in TUM, KITTI, EuRoC and ROS bag formats.
why_it_matters: Every hackathon claim about drift needs numbers; evo produces them in minutes.
hackathon_notes: `pip install evo`. Use `evo_ape` with `-as` for monocular scale alignment.

name: rpg_trajectory_evaluation
summary: Toolbox for quantitative trajectory evaluation of VO/VIO, implementing the alignment and relative-error protocol from Zhang & Scaramuzza (IROS 2018).
why_it_matters: Reference for how to evaluate VIO properly by segment length.
hackathon_notes: Works without ROS; evo is easier day to day.

name: Kalibr
summary: Toolbox for camera intrinsic, multi-camera and camera-IMU spatial/temporal calibration.
why_it_matters: Bad calibration is the number-one reason VIO fails on custom rigs.
hackathon_notes: Use the Docker image; print an AprilGrid and record a slow, well-excited bag.

name: 14 Lectures on Visual SLAM (English)
summary: English edition of Gao Xiang's open textbook on visual SLAM, from geometry and Lie groups to back-end optimization.
why_it_matters: Best free practical intro for a team ramping up on SLAM in a weekend.
hackathon_notes: PDF and code exercises (slambook2 repo).
